headline: 22,721 passengers affected as 159 Dhaka-Riyadh flights cancelled
summary: Massive flight cancellations on the route between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia have left thousands of travelers stranded.
details: A total of 159 flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled, causing significant disruption to air travel.
Over 22,721 passengers have been affected by these sudden cancellations on the route.
The cancellations have created logistical challenges for thousands of travelers moving between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia.

headline: 1.27mn students await HSC results this Saturday
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results at 11am, with online and SMS options available for examinees.
details: Over 1.27 million students who sat for the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are waiting for their results, which will be published this Saturday.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results at 11am at the conference room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division under the Ministry of Education.
Students can check their results through their educational institutions, online portals, or via SMS. The Inter-Board Coordination Committee has confirmed that preparations are nearly complete.
A total of 1,270,583 students participated in the exams, which began on July 2 across 2,697 centres nationwide.
Students have expressed anxiety over their performance, particularly in English, and some have raised concerns about errors in Physics and Chemistry question papers.
Those dissatisfied with their results can apply for re-checking of answer scripts from November 1 to November 7 via an online portal, with a fee of Tk 150 per subject.
Students who fail the examinations will be given the opportunity to retake the exams within two months of the results being published.
caption:
Over 1.27 million students are on edge as the HSC results are set to be released this Saturday!

Over 1.27 million students who sat for the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are waiting for their results, which will be published this Saturday.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results at 11am at the conference room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division under the Ministry of Education.

Students can check their results through their educational institutions, online portals, or via SMS. The Inter-Board Coordination Committee has confirmed that preparations are nearly complete.

A total of 1,270,583 students participated in the exams, which began on July 2 across 2,697 centres nationwide.

Students have expressed anxiety over their performance, particularly in English, and some have raised concerns about errors in Physics and Chemistry question papers.

Those dissatisfied with their results can apply for re-checking of answer scripts from November 1 to November 7 via an online portal, with a fee of Tk 150 per subject.

Students who fail the examinations will be given the opportunity to retake the exams within two months of the results being published.
